# Introduction

TODO: Explain why initial soil and litter states may affect Virtual Ecosystem

The analysis estimates **global Sobol sensitivity indices**. It varies the
selected inputs simultaneously across their specified ranges; it is not a
local or Morris screening analysis.

## Research questions

- Which sampled soil and litter initial-state variables explain the most
  variation in the selected model outputs?
- How much of that influence is attributable to interactions, as indicated by
  the difference between first-order and total-order indices?

# Methods

## Scope and fixed inputs

The current scope is soil and litter initial states with the Maliau site data.
Climate variables are treated as prescribed forcings, not sampled initial
states, because their future values are specified over time. Other modules are
held fixed; where their data vary spatially, the preparation script currently
uses spatial means. Plant input data are spatially constant in this dataset.

TODO: Confirm whether elevation remains fixed and document why the selected
soil and litter states are the only sampled inputs.

## Input bounds and Sobol design

The current draft uses the minimum and maximum observed values in the source
soil and litter arrays as uniform bounds, then rescales a quasi-random Sobol
design to those bounds. The variables are sampled independently.

TODO: Confirm that observed extrema are defensible bounds, that independent

and any convergence or bootstrap checks here.

```{r}
#| label: read-sobol-matrix
project_root <- here::here()
sobol_matrix_path <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data/sensitivity/soil_litter_inputs/data/sobol_matrix.rds"
)
sobol_mat <- readRDS(sobol_matrix_path)
pars <- colnames(sobol_mat)
n_samples <- nrow(sobol_mat) / (length(pars) + 2)

if (n_samples != as.integer(n_samples)) {
  stop("Sobol matrix row count is inconsistent with its parameter count.")
}
n_samples <- as.integer(n_samples)

# TODO: Confirm the output index and matching run-truncation threshold.
analysis_time_index <- 24
```

## Model runs and output processing

Each Sobol row becomes one single-cell VE run. The PBS array selects the
matching generated soil/litter NetCDF input; VE is run from the project `uv`
lock using the latest pinned PyPI release. The run outputs are Zarr stores and
are tidied with the shared Zarr helpers before sensitivity indices are
calculated. The current runner truncates the model after update 24 to avoid
computing beyond the selected output index.

TODO: Confirm whether update 24 is the intended endpoint or only a diagnostic
time. Keep the report's `analysis_time_index` and the runner's truncation
threshold in sync. Record the VE version and any failed or repeated runs before
interpreting the indices.

From the repository root, restore the R environment once, then run the
preparation, model, and post-processing stages in order:

```bash
Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
mkdir -p analysis/soil/sensitivity/input_data/pbs_logs
qsub analysis/soil/sensitivity/input_data/build_data_and_config.sh
bash analysis/soil/sensitivity/input_data/submit_ve_array.sh
qsub analysis/soil/sensitivity/input_data/post_process_outputs.sh
```

The submit script syncs the locked Python environment before submission, derives
the array size from the generated Sobol matrix, and refuses to reuse an output
directory. The per-run directory name follows the current HPC array convention
(`array_subJob_<index>`); each job selects its input data file from the same
one-based array index.

## Output definition and aggregation

The current code uses each output variable at one selected time index. The
model configuration reduces the grid to one cell, so no spatial aggregation is
currently applied to the output.

## Sobol index calculation

First-order (`Si`) and total-order (`Ti`) indices are calculated for each
eligible output. Total-order indices include interactions with other inputs;
pairwise second-order indices are not currently requested.

```{r}
#| label: read-merged-data
#| cache: true
merged_path <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data/sensitivity/soil_litter_inputs/out/all_continuous_data_merged.parquet"
)
merged <- open_dataset(merged_path) |> collect()
```

```{r}
#| label: calc-sobol-indices
#| cache: true
#| dependson: ["read-merged-data", "read-sobol-matrix"]
Y_vars <- unique(merged$variable) |>
  setdiff(c("timestamp", "x", "y"))

sobol_results <- map(
  Y_vars,
  \(Y_var) {
    output_data <-
      merged |>
      filter(
        variable == Y_var,
        time_index == analysis_time_index
      ) |>
      select(scenario, value) |>
      arrange(scenario)

    if (nrow(output_data) != nrow(sobol_mat) ||
      anyDuplicated(output_data$scenario) > 0) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "Expected one output per Sobol scenario for %s.",
        Y_var
      ))
    }

    Y <- output_data$value
    if (anyNA(Y)) {
      stop(sprintf("Output %s contains missing values.", Y_var))
    }
    if (any(!is.finite(Y))) {
      stop(sprintf("Output %s contains non-finite values.", Y_var))
    }
    if (var(Y) == 0) {
      message("Skipping output with no variation: ", Y_var)
      return(NULL)
    }

    sobol_indices(Y = Y, N = n_samples, params = pars)
  }
)
names(sobol_results) <- Y_vars

sens <-
  imap(
    sobol_results,
    \(result, Y_var) {
      if (is.null(result)) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      as_tibble(result$results) |> mutate(Y_var = Y_var)
    }
  ) |>
  list_rbind()
```

## Overall sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: fig-overall
#| dependson: "calc-sobol-indices"
#| fig-cap: "Placeholder: total-order Sobol indices for each output."
#| column: screen
#| crop: true
sens_total <- sens |> filter(sensitivity == "Ti")

sens_total |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_raster(aes(y = parameters, x = Y_var, fill = original)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "cividis",
    transform = "sqrt",
    name = "Total-order index"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Output variable", y = "Input variable") +
  coord_fixed(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3, angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 3),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

total-order indices. Choose an output after reviewing the overall results.
